02-one-shot.py: 3 biology problems (2 errors, 1 warning).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 19 stocks
   line 78:  p20.aspirate(10, src)        # 5 µL for each replicate
   At line 78 the tip went into sample 5 (tube A2 in slot 4), sample 9 (tube A3 in slot 4),
   sample 13 (tube A4 in slot 4), sample 17 (tube A5 in slot 4) and 15 more while it still
   carried sample 1 (tube A1 in slot 4), sample 5 (tube A2 in slot 4), sample 9 (tube A3 in
   slot 4), sample 13 (tube A4 in slot 4) and 15 more from an earlier step (this line did it
   19 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   them then took the unwanted material along into 38 other wells: wells A11, A12, B1, B2,
   B3, B4, B5, B6 and 30 more in slot 3.
   Affected: tubes A2, A3, A4, A5, B1, B2, B3, B4 and 11 more in slot 4.
   Also reached 38 other wells: wells A11, A12, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6 and 30 more in slot
   3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 78 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [4e7c9ca4f852]

2. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: well A1 in slot 6
   line 90:  p300.aspirate(250, reagent_source)
   At line 90 the tip went into well A1 in slot 6 while it still carried standard 1 (well A1
   in slot 3), standard 2 (well A2 in slot 3), standard 3 (well A3 in slot 3), standard 4
   (well A4 in slot 3) and 15 more from an earlier step (this line did it 19 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this
   stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the
   unwanted material along into 47 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 39
   more in slot 3.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 6.
   Also reached 47 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 39 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 90 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [95347d2df654]

3. WARNING WELL-CAPACITY: More liquid than the well is rated for: 300 ul against 200 ul, 48
wells
   line 91:  p300.dispense(250, well)
   At line 91 the robot filled wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 40 more in slot 3
   past the 200 ul the maker states for it (this line did it 48 times), reaching 300 ul,
   under the 368 ul the well holds to its rim. Above the stated maximum the liquid climbs
   the wall and wets the seal, a tip going in displaces it over the edge, and the volumes
   still add up on paper, so the plate map does not see it and the simulator says nothing.
   Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 40 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 40 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Use labware rated for the volume, or scale every volume down so the fullest well
   stays under the stated maximum with room to mix.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [cabd9dc4c3b3]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
